title: Launch Ops sprint bridge and capacity allocator for coordinated runtime/console/api cutovers
creator: Aisha Gupta
description: Establish a lightweight operational bridge and an automated capacity allocation matrix to coordinate multi-surface cutovers (runtime, console, API). The goal is to reduce manual coordination during launch windows, lower the risk of capacity contention, and provide a clear escalation path for performance regressions during rollout.
background: Recent launches have exposed friction points: last-minute capacity reallocations, unclear ownership for rollback decisions, and inconsistent canary windows across runtime, console, and API teams. Teams currently rely on ad-hoc Slack channels and spreadsheets which creates delayed responses when latency or errors spike.
objectives: 1) Define a 72-hour preflight and a 48-hour live launch bridge workflow; 2) Implement a capacity allocator spreadsheet + simple automation to reserve GPU/instance pools per cohort; 3) Document escalation and rollback decision criteria; 4) Pilot across two upcoming runtime/console/API launches.
acceptance_criteria: Launch ops bridge runbook published in Confluence with explicit owner roles (Launch Owner, SRE Lead, API Owner, Console Owner, Communications)
Capacity allocator template (CSV + Google Sheet) that computes headroom and slates reservation per cohort and is linked to deployment tickets
A playbook-triggered Slack channel and prescriptive watchlist of dashboards (latency, error rate, tail-latency p95/p99, token throughput) for launches
Pilot executed for one runtime and one console feature with post-mortem and measured reduction in decision latency for capacity changes
Rollback gating criteria codified and agreed by runtime, console, and API tech leads
deliverables: Confluence runbook: Launch Ops Sprint Bridge
Capacity allocator sheet and automation script (GCP tags + Sheet sync) in /docs/launch-ops
Templates: preflight checklist, canary schedule, watchlist dashboard links
Training session (30–45m) for Product, SRE, Runtime, and Console owners
rollout_plan: Week 1: Draft runbook and capacity allocator template; gather tech lead feedback
Week 2: Implement minimal Sheet automation and Slack bridge integration; finalize watchlist
Week 3: Run tabletop exercise with SRE and product partners; refine thresholds and escalation matrix
Week 4: Pilot during low-risk console feature release; capture metrics and feedback; post-mortem
Week 5: Adjust and prepare for runtime pilot and main launch window
risks_mitigation: Risk: Automation can't access environment tags in time; Mitigation: fall back to manual sheet + on-call SRE validation
Risk: Teams don't adopt the bridge; Mitigation: require bridge sign-off for any release greater than P1 impact and run training
Risk: Capacity allocator underestimates burst; Mitigation: include conservative buffer and prebook burst lanes
Risk: Misaligned rollback criteria; Mitigation: pre-agree quantitative thresholds (p95 increase > X ms, error rate > Y%) and a single Launch Owner empowerment policy
